result:
I found 11 rules in `pricebook.py` that didn't match their docstrings and fixed all of them. To check, I compared all 150 rules against a reference built from each docstring and the module's shared rules, over a range of quantity and unit-price combinations. 11 differed before the fix and none differ now.

| Rule | What was wrong | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 03, 107 | The cap only applied when the discount was over 60,000 won | Always cap the discount |
| 19 | A "whole" rule computed the discount only on units above the threshold | Discount the full amount (`base`) |
| 66 | Same problem as rule 19 | Discount the full amount (`base`) |
| 68 | A "marginal" rule discounted the full amount | Discount only units above the threshold |
| 29, 48 | The cap was applied to the amount before the discount, not to the discount | Calculate the discount, then cap it |
| 139 | The cap was applied to the price, not to the discount | Calculate the discount, then cap it |
| 54 | Used `round`, so discounts were rounded instead of cut down to the won | Changed to `// 100` |
| 59, 71 | Used `>` instead of `>=`, so exactly 10 or 20 units got no discount | Changed to `>=` |

I also changed rule 121's `qty >= 51` to `>= 50`. That one was harmless: at exactly 50 units a marginal discount is 0 either way, so the result doesn't change. I changed it so the code says what the docstring says.

STATUS: DONE
